statement: A caterer has at most $300$ minutes to prepare sandwiches and salads for an event. Each sandwich takes $4$ minutes to prepare and each salad takes $6$ minutes. The order must include at least $20$ salads. What is the greatest number of sandwiches the caterer can prepare?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the 20 salads from the 300 minutes as if each salad took 1 minute, so I got $280 \div 4 = 70$.
I divided all 300 minutes by 4 minutes per sandwich and forgot that the 20 salads need time too.
I added the 120 minutes for the salads to the 300 minutes instead of subtracting them, so I got $420 \div 4 = 105$.

hints: To make as many sandwiches as possible, make as few salads as allowed.
With $s$ sandwiches and $20$ salads, the time used is $4s + 6(20)$, which must be at most $300$.
The salads take $6 \times 20 = 120$ minutes, leaving $180$ minutes for sandwiches.

solutions.reliable: Let $s$ be the number of sandwiches and $d$ the number of salads, with $4s + 6d \le 300$ and $d \ge 20$. Sandwiches are largest when $d = 20$: $4s + 120 \le 300$, so $4s \le 180$ and $s \le 45$. Check: $4(45) + 6(20) = 300$ minutes exactly.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
